dimensions.assessment: Applies primarily to the Department of Commerce, specific congressional committees, and entities submitting export applications or located in Country Group D:5.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative reporting and transparency requirements without changing underlying export restrictions.
dimensions.evidence: requires the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to annually report to Congress on export control licensing.

dimensions.assessment: Subject to the availability of appropriations, with no specific dollar amounts or funding changes stated.
dimensions.evidence: subject to the availability of appropriations

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to add specific reporting mandates.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1756 of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4815) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent annual reporting requirement starting not later than one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this subsection, and not less frequently than annually thereafter

missing_information: Exact costs or budgetary impact of preparing the reports.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security to submit annual reports to specific congressional committees regarding certain export control licensing, end-use checks, and related activities concerning covered entities, while maintaining information confidentiality and protecting ongoing investigations.
